author: Kathryn Bruch
title: Chlamydia cases in Mobile County continue to rise this year - NewsBreak
text:
By Kathryn Bruch ,
1 hours ago
MOBILE, Ala. ( WKRG ) — Chlamydia remains the most frequently reported sexually transmitted disease in Mobile County, and health officials expect this year’s case total to increase from 2025.
Manslaughter case of Air Force Airman denied a motion for dismissal The Mobile County Health Department reported 77 cases last week, bringing the county’s total to 1,915 so far in 2026. Health Officer Dr. Kevin Michaels said MCHD reported almost 3,200 cases in 2025.
PROVISIONAL DISEASE REPORT – CHLAMYDIA CASES Download “The only way you’re going to get chlamydia is through unprotected sexual activity,” Michaels said. “It’s based on the sexual practice of the individual and, yes, unprotected sex multiple partners increases the risk.”
Michaels said young women make up most of Mobile’s reported cases.
“The vast majority of cases have been in the female population. So, women, and typically in the age range of 10 to 29,” Michaels said.
According to Alabama Public Health’s STD report , 6,490 chlamydia cases were reported across the state from Jan. through Mar. 2026.
Michaels said increased testing may be one reason more cases are being reported each year.
Historic Oakleigh House Museum in Mobile closes for major repairs: what to know “I think more people are getting tested. It’s present. The availability of treatment is available,” Michaels said.
The infection may be difficult to detect because symptoms can differ between men and women.
“Women, you can have chlamydia and not know about it. It’s present. It may not cause any symptoms,” Michaels said. “Men are going to experience symptoms. They’re going to experience burning when they pass through urine.”
Michaels urged anyone experiencing symptoms to contact a primary care provider for testing. Chlamydia can be treated with antibiotics.
